author: Brigid Brown
title: Trump 'shamefully' lines White House walls with pictures of him with autocrats - NewsBreak
text:
By Brigid Brown ,
4 hours ago Donald Trump is up to his old tricks, giving the White House the Mar-a-Lago treatment, which now includes photos of him with recent guests.
MS NOW ’s Jacqueline Alemany shared photos of the White House walls with new wallhangings featuring Trump with Vladimir Putin and XI Jinping. She shared the photos to X with a caption that read, “White House's Palm Room doors now lined with photos of Trump standing alongside Putin & Xi.”
The tweet went viral soon after, garnering 515K views and 2.1K likes in a matter of hours.

• Trump throws a glass of water in middle of his speech and says 'it's ridiculous'
It seemed like some people were fine with the changes and others were not, sharing their opinions in the comments section.
@_Britt_Martinez wrote: “Republican or Democrat, no U.S. president should display framed photos of dictators in the White House. It’s an insult to the democratic values that office is supposed to represent.”
Kelan Craig shared a post on X that said, “They are not our allies. This administration cannot be gone fast enough.”
There were people who suggested it may be strategic, with one X user writing, “The admin is correct to posture like they are allies.”
And another X user asking, “Why can’t China and Russia be America’s allies?”
Theresa Sanders may be the tiebreaker, writing in the same thread that there is no such thing as an ally: “Our Allies aren’t our Allies! Remember Kissinger’s words? To the effect that it was Dangerous to be an Enemy of the USA, but Deadly to be its Ally!” she wrote.
X user @rpmjrOM saw something else, making a powerful statement with just four words: “The men he admires.”
Trump hosted Vladimir Putin in Alaska on Aug. 15, 2025. The historic 2025 Russia-United States Summit took place at Joint Base Elmendorf–Richardson in Anchorage, Alaska.
More recently, Trump hosted President Xi for an official three-day state visit in Washington, D.C.. This marked Xi's first visit to the White House in over a decade.
For many, Trump hosting dictators was a shock, but for Trump, it appears to be a flex that he is able to command their respect, which could, in turn, play a role in negotiating.
